title: A Month in Space Makes You 2.5 cm Taller
hook: Without gravity the spine stretches, and astronauts grow taller
summary: After about a month in weightlessness, height increases by roughly 2.5 cm, and tears cannot flow but ball up instead.

text: An astronaut watches a drink float inside the space station.
Strange things happen to the body up here too.
On Earth, gravity presses on your spine all day.
You are a bit taller after a night lying down
because that pressure eases for a while.
In space this pressure is gone altogether.
After about a month, height goes up by roughly 2.5 cm.

panels.text: If I went to space I could be a basketball player

text: An astronaut floating aboard the station.
With nothing to hold up, the bones do less work too.
an average loss of 1 to 2 percent a month was recorded.
Even if you cry, the tears don't run down.
They stick together and ball up.

panels.text: So in space you can cry and your face stays dry

sources: Wikipedia: Effect of spaceflight on the human body
